prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop homepage comp for fcullmann.com, approximately 1440 × 1000 landscape
Primary request: Design a bespoke public portfolio-and-tools homepage for Florian Ullmann using the visual logic of a modern browser performance waterfall. It must feel like an authored website for a senior engineer, not a DevTools screenshot. The focal task is a real JSON formatter operation that visibly progresses from editable input through formatting and validation to clean output across the main timing timeline.
Scene/backdrop: An edge-to-edge off-white website canvas organized by a fine timing ruler, crisp horizontal traces, phase markers, status transitions, and subtle focus depth. Treat performance-inspector conventions as an editorial design system: simplified, intentional, approachable, and clearly navigable as a public website.
Subject: Compact horizontal navigation at the top with an understated fcullmann.com wordmark. A narrow left timing rail contains the bold identity “Florian Ullmann — Senior Software Engineer” and a short plain-language introduction about building useful, durable software. In the main area, show an immediately usable JSON formatter: plausible editable JSON input, a prominent “Format JSON” action, staged trace labels such as Parse, Validate, Format, and Ready, then a clean formatted JSON output with indentation, syntax color, line numbers, valid status, and copy affordance. Show the operation as one continuous input-to-output performance trace without sacrificing normal form usability. Near the lower edge, “Featured tools” crosses the fold as ranked, inspectable traces including “01 JSON Formatter”, “02 Base64”, and “03 UUID Generator”. Below that, reveal the beginning of “Latest writing”.
Style/medium: polished high-fidelity desktop web UI screenshot; contemporary editorial systems design; precise, calm, highly usable; subtle layering and focus depth; tight typography and purposeful information density.
Composition/framing: full-page straight-on desktop website at a 1440 × 1000-ish ratio, no browser chrome and no device frame. Compact header. Slim identity/timing rail on the left. Main interaction occupies most of the upper viewport. A horizontal millisecond ruler and trace lanes support the formatter flow. Featured tools visibly begin before the fold and continue beneath it. Maintain realistic responsive-web spacing, clear links, and accessible controls.
Lighting/mood: flat screen-native presentation with crisp foreground focus and restrained depth cues; fast, exact, dependable, quietly technical.
Color palette: off-white #F6F7F4, ink #14191F, blue #2E6CF6, coral #FF6B4A. Use blue for active states and primary action, coral for timing/status accents, and neutral grays for inactive trace phases. No gradients.
Materials/textures: clean digital surfaces, hairline rules, subtle soft shadows only where needed to clarify focus and interaction; no glossy effects.
Text (verbatim): “fcullmann.com”; “Florian Ullmann — Senior Software Engineer”; “I build useful, durable software for the web.”; “Tools that earn their tab.”; “JSON input”; “Format JSON”; “Parse”; “Validate”; “Format”; “Ready”; “Valid JSON”; “Copy”; “Featured tools”; “01 JSON Formatter”; “02 Base64”; “03 UUID Generator”; “Latest writing”.
Constraints: English language. Render required text exactly and legibly. Make the formatter genuinely look editable, usable, and already responding live. The timing visualization must reinforce the input-to-output operation rather than obscure it. Include compact public-site navigation, clear affordances, believable JSON, strong hierarchy, accessible contrast, crisp alignment, and one memorable scale contrast in the identity.
Avoid: literal DevTools screenshot, Bootstrap cards, generic SaaS dashboard, portrait photography, fake metrics or vanity statistics, gradients, terminal cliché, black hacker aesthetic, illegible decorative text, ornamental gibberish, excessive microtext, browser chrome, device frame, watermark, poster-only composition.
